newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: LatAm energy group seeks private-sector partners.
newsitem.headline: LatAm energy group seeks private-sector partners.

text.p: Government members of the Latin American Energy Organization (OLADE) will work to involve business with the organization, the group's new secretary general said at the end of the OLADE's 27th meeting on Friday.

"It is immediately necessary to strongly promote the activities and objectives of the organization in the private sector so that it becomes part of our projects," Luis Augusto Fonseca told reporters this week during meetings here.
Fonseca said OLADE will work through energy ministries and business groups in member countries to publicize the organization and attract business members.

Fonseca, chief of international relations for Petrobras, Brazil's state-owned oil company, was elected to a three-year term as secretary general of OLADE Friday by energy ministers from 25 Latin American nations.
OLADE is a public cooperation agency that promotes the integration of energy resources in the region.

Latin American and Caribbean nations produce 8.9 percent of the world's power, including petroleum, natural gas and nuclear and hydroelectric energy, and they represent 6.7 percent of global energy consumption.

Representatives of the five Central America nations and Panama met Wednesday to discuss forming a multinational company to develop, design, finance, construct and maintain a regional network to connect their electric systems.
Supporters of the project say they hope the network will be functional within five years and will lower consumer electric prices in the region by 10 percent.

Guatemala's minister of energy, Leonel Lopez, elected for a one-year term as president of OLADE, told reporters that representatives from Guatemala and Canada met this week to discuss Canadian investment in Guatemala hydroelectric projects.
Lopez said Mexican delegates were also in Guatemala, exploring the possibility of building a pipeline for natural gas that would be for sale in Guatemala and Central America.
